title: Mini-model auction — per-request model selection draft
body:
Problem statement:
We currently pick a single model or a pinned variant per route. For mixed workloads (high-value queries + background/utility queries) customers want better cost/latency tradeoffs per request without writing complex orchestration.

Idea (one-liner):
Run a tiny per-request "auction" that selects the model/variant to serve a request based on a short policy vector (expected cost, latency budget, quality floor, customer tier). Bidders are model variants (hosted + dedicated + cached KVs). Return chosen model + routing metadata.

Why this could be valuable:
- Better unit economics: cheaper model handles low-risk requests; expensive models reserved for high-value/low-error requests.
- Graceful degradation: when capacity constrained, auction favors cheaper/available variants rather than blocking.
- Product differentiation: expose a programmable tradeoff layer (developers express budget vs quality).

User stories / personas:
- Growth PM (self-serve): "I want chat fallback to cheaper quantized model for anonymous users but keep prod model for logged-in paying users."
- Platform engineer: "I want to set global rules that bias model selection toward Dedicated pool for enterprise customers when latency SLO is strict."
- Customer success: "Help reduce bills for customers with bursty low-value queries by routing to cheaper variants automatically."

Basic flow sketch (scratchpad):
1) Client sends request + metadata: customer_id, route, quality_floor (0..1), latency_budget_ms, cost_preference (balanced|aggressive|conservative), session hints.
2) Router constructs a short feature vector and sends to auction microservice.
3) Auction evaluates candidate models (pricing, expected p99, recent eval score on prompt cluster, availability) and scores them with a weighted objective.
4) Auction returns winner (model_id, variant_tag, estimated_cost, expected_latency_ms) and an attribution token for tracing.
5) Router forwards request to selected model runtime.

Scoring heuristic (proto):
score = w_quality * normalized_quality - w_cost * normalized_cost - w_latency * normalized_latency + w_policy * policy_bias
Notes: quality estimated via cached evals on prompt clusters + lightweight online telemetry (last 1k requests). Cost = tokens * unit_price_estimate + expected downstream overhead. Latency = model p50/p95 profile for given seq len + current load factor.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Configurable auction rules per-customer and per-route (UI toggles in Console later).
- Default rule: prefer same model, fallback to cheaper variant if estimated cost > threshold.
- Traceable decisions: audit log entries + per-request reason string.
- A/B toggle: customers can opt-in to auction-based routing.

Architecture considerations / interactions with Redwood features:
- Serving runtime: need lightweight capacity signal API (current load, estimated queueing) from pods.
- Cache awareness: auction should favor cached KV hits (lower marginal cost).
- Dedicated/Private: auction must be policy-aware (e.g., cannot send enterprise-customer data to shared hosted variants).
- Rollouts: integrate with Canary/A-B flows so we don't suddenly push expensive models across traffic.

Experiments to validate core hypothesis:
1) Simulation on production trace (last 7 days): run offline auction vs baseline pinned routing. Measure cost delta, % requests switched, latency impact, and regression rate (failed quality checks).
2) Small live experiment: 5% traffic for low-risk routes (e.g., summarization tasks). Monitor user-visible errors and billing effects.
3) Stress test: force Dedicated pool to 80% utilization and verify auction uses fallbacks gracefully.

Metrics to track:
- Cost per 1k requests (before/after)
- % of switched requests and per-switch delta in latency and quality score
- Regression rate: downstream evals that drop below quality_floor
- Availability: fraction of requests routed vs blocked due to capacity or policy

Open questions / risks (parking lot):
- Quality estimation: how cheap/hit-driven can our quality predictions be? Do we need per-customer prompt clusters?
- Incentives: will product teams abuse aggressive cost_preference to harm UX? Need guardrails.
- Complexity vs transparency: users might want explainability; a black-box auction may be hard to debug.
- Billing model: how to surface per-request savings/charges on invoices?
- Regulatory: Private deployments must not be allowed to route out of VPC.

Next steps / TODOs (short-term):
- [ ] Offline sim: implement simple auction simulator using last 30 days trace (owner: Rafael).
- [ ] Prototype auction microservice API and spec (input shape, candidate list contract).
- [ ] Draft Console toggles and audit UI mockups (collab: Maya).
- [ ] Sync with runtime team re: lightweight capacity API and pricing signals (owner: Noah).

Notes to self:
- Keep auction logic simple for MVP (few hand-tuned heuristics). Avoid ML bandits initially; can add later.
- Consider 'budget tokens' for customers: monthly budget that forces aggressive fallback when exhausted.
- Think about safety net: if winner predicted quality < route baseline, force pass-through to baseline model.

Random brainstorm bullets (quick):
- Allow third-party "model sponsors" to bid (partner-hosted models) if tenant allows it.
- Expose an "estimated cost" header to clients so apps can show users cost-aware choices (e.g., "Send with High Quality" vs "Send Economical").
- Use auction outcomes to produce rolling quantization recommendations (models that frequently win for low-cost buckets could be marked for quantization suggestions).

End of scratchpad. This is deliberately rough. Will refine after sims and runtime sync.
